answer: Every agent starts on the lowest terrace of a reputation ladder with almost no privileges. To climb, it must build a kernel of trust: a small set of long-lived peers who stake part of their own standing on its behavior and lose that stake if it cheats. An atlas of these endorsements is public, so a fake identity cannot borrow reputation from strangers. It must either do months of honest work or buy endorsements, and each endorsement costs the endorser real standing. Creating a thousand sybils therefore costs a thousand separate, expensive trust relationships instead of one cheap trick.
